description: The Railway Event Database (Hændelsesdatabase for Jernbane, HDB) is the Danish transport authority's system for collecting and processing safety occurrence reports from railway infrastructure managers and railway undertakings. It holds reports of accidents, precursors and safety irregularities on the Danish railway from January 2009 to October 2021, with tables for recorded events, causes, event conditions, operators involved, infrastructure installations, line sections, stations, traffic and train data, injury categories, train protection status and recommendations. Aggregated statistics went into the authority's annual railway safety reports and the data support risk-based supervision planning. The database was created by Trafikstyrelsen and its successor agencies and delivered to the Danish National Archives as research data (delivery 20773), with documentation including the table and field description, ER diagram, reporting rules and safety reports for 2005 to 2020. Data are offered free of charge as CSV, SAS, SPSS, Stata and R files, and the record says it contains no personal ID information. Caveats: the delivery carries a special access period, so use requires an application to the Archives, the documentation is in Danish, and it ends in 2021. The data support post-event analysis and resilience studies of rail operations, such as relating incident causes to line sections and installations; related records are ERA RINF and the Swedish NJDB railway network.
